sections.title: Your team learns the same thing four times
body: Four developers, four assistants, the same correction typed four times: reuse the rate limiter. Each assistant is taught separately, and each lesson stays where it was learned.
sections.caption: The same lesson, four times.

sections.title: Start with your own constitution
body: Even working alone you have a constitution: the rules Sensei follows on your projects. Some you write, some it learns from your corrections, and some come from proven rule packs you adopt.
Your own rules stay yours. A dōjō is optional, and joining one doesn’t take them away.

sections.title: Share it, on your terms
body: When a rule works for you, you can offer it to your dōjō. You see exactly what would be shared first: the rule itself and counts as evidence, never code or transcripts, with origin details like repository names stripped. Nothing goes until you confirm.

sections.title: The team decides what becomes a rule
body: Contributions from members accumulate: four people offering versions of the same lesson become one candidate with the evidence of all four. Maintainers triage and approve it, and then it is distributed.

sections.title: It comes back as an upgrade
body: Every member receives the approved rule as an upgrade, and each decides: apply it, mute it, or pin it. Applied, it joins their constitution and their assistant loads it from the next session.

sections.title: The right rules, in every repository
body: Rules live at three levels in a dōjō: the dōjō itself, a workspace (a group of repositories) and a single repository, alongside your personal rules. You sign in once, and Sensei resolves the effective rules for every repository you touch.
You can preview, for any project, exactly which rules govern it and why, before the first commit. How conflicts are settled is covered in “Which rule wins?”.

takeaway: Learn it once. The team keeps it.
takeawaySub: Sensei and your dōjō, sharing on your terms.
